problems.title: Which three-dimensional constant-width body has least volume?
problems.statement_md: Among all convex bodies in $\mathbb R^3$ of width one, is the minimum volume $\pi[2/3-(\sqrt3/4)\arccos(1/3)]$, attained by the Meissner tetrahedra? In everyday terms: which solid that fits exactly between parallel planes one unit apart in every orientation uses the least material?
problems.hint_md: Start by computing the candidate tetrahedron’s exact volume and comparing area through Blaschke’s identity. This is an entry point, not a known route to a full proof.

problems.title: Does the Reuleaux triangle have the highest fundamental frequency?
problems.statement_md: For planar convex bodies $K$ of constant width one, is the first Dirichlet Laplace eigenvalue always at most that of the Reuleaux triangle? Equivalently: among equally wide membranes fixed along their boundary, does the Reuleaux triangle have the highest fundamental vibration frequency (with the same material parameters)?
problems.hint_md: Compare the Rayleigh-quotient formulation with the known Cheeger and inradius extrema. Identify why these bounds alone do not imply the desired eigenvalue ordering.

open_status.evidence: 2025 author preprint presents the constant-width spectral claim as numerically motivated; targeted web search found no proof.
open_status.qualification: Open status is supported by the cited discussion and search, with a weaker recency basis than the Meissner entry.

problems.title: Can extra essential generating points ever lower optimal Meissner volume?
problems.statement_md:
Let $Y\subsetneq X\subset\mathbb R^3$ be finite sets of diameter one, with $2|Y|-2$ and $2|X|-2$ diametric pairs respectively. Assume that every point of $X$ belongs to at least three such pairs; this is called a critical extremal base. Use the broad Meissner construction that allows arbitrary extremal bases, not only the standard strongly critical ones. For each base $Z$, let $S_{\min}(Z)$ be the least area among its dual-edge smoothing choices. Must
$$S_{\min}(X)\geq S_{\min}(Y)$$
hold? By the unit-width area–volume identity, this is also the corresponding question for least volume.
problems.hint_md: Begin with degree-two deletion and compare it with the first configurations having no degree-two points. The counting exercise isolates which extensions can occur.

sources.locator: Problem prob:comparison and subsequent refinements; compare arXiv:2608.19747

open_status.evidence: Explicitly posed as a problem in Intermediary_Points_Meissner.tex; dangling-point preprint checked separately.
open_status.qualification: Status is relative to the supplied research notes; broader inclusion monotonicity has not been verified by an exhaustive literature review.

problems.title: Does the Reuleaux triangle minimize total pairwise distance?
problems.statement_md: Among planar convex bodies $K$ of constant width one, does the Reuleaux triangle minimize $E(K)=\int_K\int_K|x-y|\,dx\,dy$? This is the unnormalized total distance over all pairs of material points, not the mean distance $E(K)/|K|^2$.
problems.hint_md: Keep the energy unnormalized. Test the triangle against regular and irregular Reuleaux polygons, and separate numerical evidence from any proposed global inequality.

sources.locator: README and pair-energy sections of reuleaux_kernels.tex

open_status.evidence: The source README explicitly says the pure distance-kernel minimum remains unproved.
open_status.qualification: Literature-wide novelty and status have not been established.
